contexts.text: Gog () = those who apprehend doctrinal things from external things with which they destroy internal worship.
Gog, and the land of Magog () = worship in externals.

In this chapter () the subject treated of is external worship separated from internal and made idolatrous, which is here signified by Gog, Meshech and Tubal, by whom are also understood doctrinal things which they take up and then confirm from the literal sense of the Word, and thus falsify truths, and destroy internal worship; for, when thus spoken of, opposite things are signified by the same nations.

Gog and Magog () = those who are in external worship without internal, and thus made idolatrous. AC 2928:3. AC 3240:6. AC 3355:3. AC 3448:9. AC 3708:21. AC 4236:3. AC 4715:5. DSS 18:3. AE 257. AE 355:20. AE 357:31. AE 388:14. AE 400:9. AE 578:6. AE 644:26. AE 650:41. AE 1061:3.
Gog = external worship separated from internal; thus, those who place everything of Divine worship in external things, when charity has been extinguished.
Gog and Magog () = those who are in external natural worship separated from internal spiritual worship. AR 859, Illustrated. AR 862.
In  those are treated of who are in the sense of the letter only, and thence in worship which is external without internal, who are Gog...
That they will come into the Church which is Gog. Signified. Their character fully described. AR 859:4.
Gog and Magog, in the Hebrew, mean a roof and a floor, thus what is external.
They who are averse to Knowledges... and who place all worship in external things, are Gog and Magog, in the Apocalypse.
On Gog and Magog. Fully described.
